conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. You're here for your 21st cycle of high-dose methotrexate. How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm okay. A little nervous, but I know the routine by now. I just hope I don’t get those headaches again like last time with Zofran.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We remember that. This time, we’re giving fosaprepitant and dexamethasone instead to prevent nausea — no Zofran — so you should avoid the headaches.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, good. That’s a relief. When will the chemo start?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll start the methotrexate infusion tonight at 6 PM. We’ll keep your urine alkalized with IV bicarbonate to protect your kidneys.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Right, I’ve had trouble with the bicarb pills before — they make me nauseous. I’m glad we’re doing it through the IV.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. We want to make this as smooth as possible. We’ll also start leucovorin 24 hours after the chemo to help clear the methotrexate safely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And my other meds — like gabapentin and citalopram — will I keep taking those?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you’ll continue both. We’ve paused your mesalamine for your colitis during the stay, but we’ll restart it when you go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And my aspirin? I know I stopped the blood thinner a while back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re on heparin shots while you’re here for clot prevention. We hold the aspirin during chemo, but you’ll restart it at discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. I just worry about the clots, with my history.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We do too, which is why we’re using heparin. You’re in good hands.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re starting the methotrexate now. It’ll take a few hours. Let us know if you feel any discomfort.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks. I’ll let you know if anything feels off.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How did you sleep? Any nausea or headaches overnight?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Not great. I had some nausea and couldn’t sleep — my mind was racing. I took the Ativan and Compazine you left for me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I’m sorry you had a rough night. The fosaprepitant usually helps, but sometimes chemo can still cause these side effects. We’ll keep an eye on it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that normal? The racing thoughts?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s not common, but some patients report mood changes or restlessness. It could be from the chemo or the medications. We’ll monitor you closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I’m feeling calmer now. Just tired.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. Your labs this morning look stable — no signs of kidney or liver issues. Your blood counts are holding up well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the methotrexate level?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll check it again today and tomorrow. So far, it’s clearing as expected. That’s a good sign.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re going to do a brain MRI today — part of your routine surveillance to check for any changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that scheduled for today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, in about an hour. It’s just to make sure there’s no recurrence. Your last one was clear, so we’re hopeful.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I hope so. I’ve been feeling okay neurologically — no weakness or dizziness.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s reassuring. Your strength and coordination still look good on exam.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news — the MRI results are back. No new lesions, no enhancement. Just stable chronic changes from before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, that’s such a relief. Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, excellent. Your methotrexate level this morning is 0.18 micromolar — that’s low enough to be safe. We can plan for discharge today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Really? That’s great. What about the leucovorin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll take a short course of oral leucovorin at home — same as last time. It’ll help finish clearing the chemo.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my other meds — everything goes back to normal?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. Restart your mesalamine, gabapentin, citalopram, and aspirin. Use your inhalers as usual. We’ll send a list with you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And if I feel nauseous again at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Use the prochlorperazine or lorazepam as needed. Call us if it’s severe or lasts more than a day or two.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll see Dr. ___ in two weeks for your next oncology check. We’ll also review your blood work then.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All set. Your discharge orders are ready. You’re doing well — keep up with your meds and rest.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Dr. Lee. I really appreciate the care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and we’ll see you soon in clinic.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do. Have a good day.
